subject.title: [Bug P2] scheduleReconnect() has no max retry limit — infinite reconnect loop

question: Should GatewayClient gain an opt-in reconnect attempt ceiling, and which callers should set it while node-host remains unbounded by default?
rationale: Current source proves the unbounded retry loop, but repository policy and node-host usage make a global cap compatibility-sensitive rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Opt-in cap for short-lived clients
options.body: Add a package-level `maxReconnectAttempts` policy and wire it only for maintainer-approved short-lived callers while preserving node-host unlimited recovery.

options.title: Global retry cap
options.body: Apply a default cap to all GatewayClient users, accepting the risk that long gateway outages can stop existing node-host workflows.

options.title: No cap, diagnostics only
options.body: Keep reconnect behavior unbounded and focus on listener cleanup, warnings, or operator diagnostics instead of changing retry policy.

recommendation.title: Opt-in cap for short-lived clients
recommendation.body: Add a package-level `maxReconnectAttempts` policy and wire it only for maintainer-approved short-lived callers while preserving node-host unlimited recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: The gateway-client extraction and current scheduler history point to steipete as the strongest available owner for the compatibility policy decision.
